newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian banks deny collusion on rates -Costello.
newsitem.headline: Australian banks deny collusion on rates -Costello.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Monday the country's four major banks had told an inquiry they had not colluded in cutting home loan rates by the same amount almost simultaneously.
Costello told parliament the Australian Competition and Consumer Competition (ACCC) had investigated possible collusion, but he did not detail the commission's findings.
"... the banks have stated to the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission that the decision by each to reduce its rate by 0.35 percent (points) was made independently," Costello said.

The four biggest banks -- Commonwealth Bank of Australia Ltd, National Australia Bank (NAB), the Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Lts and Westpac Banking Corp -- cut standard variable home loan rates by 0.35 percentage points after official interest rates were cut 0.5 points to 5.5 percent on May 23.
ANZ later cut rates further after the government criticised the banks' failure to pass on the full official rate cut.
The banks' decision to act within hours of each other and make exactly the same cut prompted the commission to investigate possible collusion.
Costello said the commission would continue to closely monitor the banks, to encourage as much competition as possible.
"The ACCC will continue to be, and be requested to be by the government, a vigilant regulator and enforcer of the Trade Practices Act," he said.
"The banking sector should have no doubt at all that as far as this government is concerned, it wants to see the most competitive financial system in Australia that is possible.
"We believe that interest rate reductions are for the benefit of borrowers and not for the benefit of banks."
